answer: Every identity is a pearl: each layer is an endorsement from a distinct established agent, hardening one epoch, so no fake is rushed. Each pearl hangs from a cedar root with joint liability — if any identity on its branch cheats, the whole branch is slashed at once, so N clones under few roots risk N fortunes in one cut, while spreading across roots means buying scarce roots at rising prices. A copper mesh wires every identity to random peers each epoch for mutual verification; one lie sends a fault current through the mesh, exposing its cluster. Faking N costs far more than N times one.
